courses.title: Introduction to Data Literacy
courses.shortDescription: An 8-week foundation course designed to help beginners understand, work with, interpret, and communicate data confidently.
courses.description:
Introduction to Data Literacy (ST-DL101) is an 8-week foundation course designed to help beginners understand, work with, interpret, and communicate data confidently. Learners explore the data lifecycle, Excel, data preparation, statistics, visualization, data ethics, and analytical thinking through practical real-world datasets, answering the core question: Can you look at data, understand what it is telling you, question it appropriately, and communicate what you found?

Assessment Structure:
• Weekly Assignments & Labs: 20%
• Mid-Course Assessment: 10%
• Final Examination: 15%
• Capstone Project: 45%
• Participation & Professional Activities: 10%
benefits: 8-step analytical workflow from questions to decisions
Hands-on Excel data preparation and cleaning
Data ethics, privacy, and bias awareness

lessons.title: What Is Data?
lessons.content:
Topics covered:
• What is data?
• Why data matters

Data consists of raw observations, measurements, facts, or signals gathered from the environment. In this lesson, we explore how data forms the raw foundation of evidence-based systems across business, healthcare, and research.

lessons.title: Data, Information and Insight
lessons.content:
Topics covered:
• Data vs information
• Information vs insight

Raw data becomes information when structured, contextualized, and organized. Information becomes actionable insight when analytical interpretation reveals meaningful patterns that guide decisions.

lessons.title: Data in Organizations and Everyday Life
lessons.content:
Topics covered:
• Why organizations use data
• Data in everyday life

Examining how institutions use data to optimize resources, assess risk, and evaluate outcomes, and how individuals interact with data in consumer and public settings.

lessons.title: Sources of Data
lessons.content:
Topics covered:
• Sources of data
• Primary data
• Secondary data

Understanding how primary data is collected directly for a specific inquiry, while secondary data leverages existing records, surveys, or published datasets.

lessons.title: Qualitative and Quantitative Data
lessons.content:
Topics covered:
• Qualitative data
• Quantitative data

Qualitative data describes characteristics, attributes, and categories, whereas quantitative data represents measurable numerical quantities.

lessons.title: Discrete and Continuous Data
lessons.content:
Topics covered:
• Discrete data
• Continuous data

Discrete data represents countable separate values, while continuous data represents measurements along an unbroken scale.

lessons.title: Categorical and Numerical Data
lessons.content:
Topics covered:
• Categorical data
• Numerical data

Grouping variables into nominal/ordinal categories versus interval/ratio numbers.

lessons.title: Structured and Unstructured Data
lessons.content:
Topics covered:
• Structured data
• Unstructured data

Contrasting relational tables, schemas, and matrices with text narratives, logs, and freeform inputs.

lessons.title: Time-Series and Cross-Sectional Data
lessons.content:
Topics covered:
• Time-series data
• Cross-sectional data

Distinguishing observations recorded over sequential time intervals from observations captured across entities at a single point in time.

lessons.title: Introduction to the Data Lifecycle
lessons.content:
Overview of the complete 7-stage lifecycle:
Collection → Storage → Preparation → Analysis → Visualization → Communication → Decision.

lessons.title: Data Collection and Storage
lessons.content:
Lifecycle stages:
• Collection
• Storage

Methods for reliable data intake and secure storage architectures.

lessons.title: Data Preparation and Analysis
lessons.content:
Lifecycle stages:
• Preparation
• Analysis

Transforming raw records into consistent datasets and applying computational techniques to answer scoped questions.

lessons.title: Visualization, Communication and Decision
lessons.content:
Lifecycle stages:
• Visualization
• Communication
• Decision

Translating analytical findings into visual displays and recommendations that inform executive decisions.

lessons.title: Reading Tables
lessons.content: How to inspect row headers, column headers, units of measure, sample totals, and data types in tabular presentations.

lessons.title: Reading Charts
lessons.content: Interpreting axes, legends, scales, and data encodings without misinterpreting the underlying values.

lessons.title: Asking Good Data Questions
lessons.content: Formulating precise, measurable questions that connect business and clinical objectives with empirical data.

lessons.title: Assumptions and Context
lessons.content:
Topics covered:
• Identifying assumptions
• Understanding context

Recognizing unstated assumptions, sampling limitations, and environmental context that frame data interpretation.

lessons.title: Identifying Misleading Information
lessons.content: Techniques for recognizing cherry-picked timeframes, truncated axes, deceptive scales, and flawed comparisons.

lessons.title: Week 1 Practical Lab: Dataset Variable Classification

Students receive a small dataset containing business, education, and healthcare examples.

Tasks:
1. Identify all variables in the dataset.
2. Classify each variable (qualitative vs quantitative, discrete vs continuous, categorical vs numerical).
3. Identify possible data sources and collection methods.
4. Develop five analytical questions that could be answered using this dataset.

Cleaning is not simply fixing cells: you must document:

• Why it was changed

Resource: Clean Dataset + Data Quality Report Template

lessons.title: Data

lessons.title: Information

lessons.title: Observation
lessons.content: Documenting objective patterns in information without speculation (e.g. waiting times are highest on Monday mornings).

lessons.title: Interpretation
lessons.content: Formulating hypotheses to explain observed patterns (e.g. Monday morning staffing may be insufficient relative to surge volume).

lessons.title: Recommendation

lessons.title: Choosing the Appropriate Chart

lessons.title: Chart Titles and Labels

lessons.title: Scale and Context

lessons.title: Avoiding Unnecessary Decoration
lessons.content: Eliminating chart junk, unnecessary 3D effects, and decorative noise to maximize data ink.

lessons.title: Misleading Visualizations

lessons.title: Privacy and Confidentiality
lessons.content: Protecting personally identifiable information (PII) and maintaining confidentiality in reporting.

lessons.title: Consent

lessons.title: Bias

lessons.title: Data Ownership

lessons.title: Why Statistics Matters
lessons.content: Understanding statistics as the language of variation, uncertainty, and evidence.

lessons.title: Descriptive Statistics
lessons.content: Summarizing, organizing, and describing characteristics of an observed dataset.

lessons.title: Inferential Statistics
lessons.content: Conceptual introduction to drawing inferences and generalizations from samples to broader populations.

lessons.title: Population and Sample
lessons.content: Defining target populations, sampling frames, representativeness, and sampling error.

lessons.title: Variable and Observation
lessons.content: Understanding data tables as matrices of observations (rows) and variables (columns).

lessons.title: Nominal
lessons.content: Nominal scale: labels and categories without intrinsic order (e.g. department, blood type, marital status).

lessons.title: Ordinal
lessons.content: Ordinal scale: ranked categories with meaningful order but unequal intervals (e.g. satisfaction ratings, education levels).

lessons.title: Interval
lessons.content: Interval scale: numerical scale with equal intervals but no true zero (e.g. Celsius temperature, calendar year).

lessons.title: Ratio
lessons.content: Ratio scale: numerical measurements with equal intervals and an absolute zero point (e.g. salary, weight, height, age).

lessons.title: Mean
lessons.content: Mathematical calculation of the arithmetic mean and its sensitivity to extreme values.

lessons.title: Median
lessons.content: Determining the middle value of ordered records and why median provides robust summaries for skewed data.

lessons.title: Mode
lessons.content: Identifying the most frequently occurring value in categorical and discrete distributions.

lessons.title: Choosing the Appropriate Measure
lessons.content: Crucial objective: The mean is not automatically the best summary. When should you use each measure based on distribution shape and measurement scale?

lessons.title: Range
lessons.content: Calculating simple range (Max - Min) and understanding its vulnerability to outliers.

lessons.title: Variance
lessons.content: Conceptual understanding of variance as average squared deviations around the mean.

lessons.title: Standard Deviation
lessons.content: Standard deviation in the original unit of measurement and interpreting spread.

lessons.title: Interquartile Range
lessons.content: Conceptual introduction to percentiles, quartiles (Q1, Q3), and the interquartile range (IQR) as a robust dispersion measure.

lessons.title: What Is an Outlier?
lessons.content: Defining outliers as data points that differ significantly from other observations in the distribution.

lessons.title: Why Outliers Matter
lessons.content: Assessing how extreme values distort the mean, inflate standard deviation, and alter model results.

lessons.title: Outlier vs Error
lessons.content: Differentiating data entry/measurement mistakes from authentic rare real-world phenomena.

lessons.title: Should an Outlier Always Be Removed?
lessons.content: Emphasizing analytical judgment: why automatically removing outliers can conceal critical insights.

lessons.title: Week 5 Practical: Calculating Statistics Manually and in Excel
lessons.content:
Practical Instructions:

Resource: Descriptive Statistics Dataset

lessons.title: Week 5 Assignment: Descriptive Statistics Report

lessons.title: Frequency
lessons.content: Constructing frequency tables and grouping data into intervals.

lessons.title: Distribution
lessons.content: Understanding the shape, spread, and center of empirical distributions.

lessons.title: Normal Distribution
lessons.content: Properties of the symmetrical bell curve and the empirical rule (68-95-99.7).

lessons.title: Skewness and Symmetry
lessons.content: Recognizing positive (right-skewed) and negative (left-skewed) distributions and their impact on mean vs median.

lessons.title: Outliers and Distribution
lessons.content: Visualizing outlier positions in boxplots and long-tailed distributions.

lessons.title: What Is Correlation?
lessons.content: Defining correlation as the statistical measure of linear association between two variables.

lessons.title: Positive Correlation
lessons.content: Understanding positive relationships where variables increase or decrease together.

lessons.title: Negative Correlation
lessons.content: Understanding inverse relationships where an increase in one variable corresponds to a decrease in another.

lessons.title: No Correlation
lessons.content: Identifying scatter plots with random distributions indicating independence.

lessons.title: Strength of Relationship
lessons.content: Interpreting correlation coefficient r from -1.0 to +1.0 conceptually.

lessons.title: Understanding Correlation
lessons.content: Reviewing observed numerical associations between variables.

lessons.title: Understanding Causation
lessons.content: Defining causality: establishing that change in one variable directly produces change in another.

lessons.title: Why Correlation Does Not Prove Causation
lessons.content: Major conceptual lesson with real-world examples: confounding variables, spurious correlations, and reverse causality.

lessons.title: Probability as Likelihood
lessons.content: Expressing likelihood on a scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

lessons.title: Simple Probability
lessons.content: Calculating basic probabilities as favorable outcomes over total possible outcomes.

lessons.title: Independent Events
lessons.content: Understanding occurrences where the outcome of one event does not influence another.

lessons.title: Dependent Events
lessons.content: Recognizing conditional scenarios where previous outcomes alter subsequent probabilities.

lessons.title: Question and Hypothesis
lessons.content: Transforming general business or health inquiries into testable hypothesis statements.

lessons.title: Evidence
lessons.content: Gathering appropriate sample evidence and establishing criteria to evaluate claims.

lessons.title: Null and Alternative Hypotheses
lessons.content: Framing the null hypothesis (status quo/no difference) against the alternative hypothesis (effect/change).

lessons.title: Statistical Significance
lessons.content: Introductory and conceptual: understanding significance as assessing whether an observation is unlikely to have occurred purely by chance.

lessons.title: Visualization and Analytical Questions

lessons.title: Distribution

lessons.title: Bar Charts

lessons.title: Line Charts

lessons.title: The 8-Step Analytics Workflow
lessons.content:
Overview of the full 8-step progression:
1. Understand: What problem are we solving?
2. Ask: What questions should the data answer?
3. Prepare: Clean and validate the dataset.
4. Analyze: Calculate relevant metrics and statistics.
5. Visualize: Create appropriate charts and dashboard.
6. Interpret: Identify meaningful findings.
7. Recommend: Translate findings into actionable recommendations.
8. Present: Communicate the results clearly.
